newsitem.title: MACAU: Activists seek to block Japan's bid for U.N. seat.
newsitem.headline: Activists seek to block Japan's bid for U.N. seat.

text.p: Activists against Japan's claim to a group of disputed isles in the East China Sea said on Monday they would attempt to block Tokyo's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council.

Thirteen activists from Hong Kong, Japan, Macau, Taiwan, Canada and Australia began a three-day meeting in Macau to prevent Tokyo from claiming the islands, known as the Diaoyus in China and Senkakus in Japan.
All but one of the activists were ethnic Chinese. One was Japanese, organisers said.

The dispute over the islands erupted in July when a right-wing Japanese youth group erected a makeshift lighthouse on one of them. The group's activities and the presence of Japanese patrol boats near the islands angered Taiwan and China and prompted protests in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau.

Participants said various activists have pooled funds to publish a full-page advertisement in The New York Times newspaper to urge the international community to block Japan's bid for the permanent U.N. seat.
"We will discuss how to unite all forces to block Japan's attempt to become a permanent member of the U.N. security council," said pro-democracy Hong Kong legislator Albert Ho.

The group, which held a news conference in the basement of a pub and karaoke bar in Portuguese-administered Macau, also said they did not rule out the possibility of attempting a new landing on the islands to protest against the Japanese presence.
Organisers said nine activists from mainland China were unable to attend the meeting because they were not granted exit permits.
